About Us
Who are we?
Northwest Collaborative Center (NWCC) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Kirkland, Washington, serving the surrounding regions.
We are an all-volunteer organization, funded entirely by public donations. NWCC is committed to increasing educational access for socioeconomically disadvantaged youth, primarily through music. We provide opportunities for these young individuals to engage in music and collaborate with fellow youth musicians.
By equipping our local communities with resources and tools, we aim to foster positive social change. We believe that through the power of music and education, we can cultivate stronger families and healthier communities.
NWCC WORKS TO IMPROVE EDUCATIONAL EQUITY
OUR ACTIVITIES
We offer weekly music instrument lessons for young people, allowing them to practice individually or as part of a chamber. Each session typically lasts 1-2 hours, during which we emphasize the importance of sharing talents and fostering gratitude through music.
Many of our program participants go on to volunteer, helping to teach new students. Building on this success, we are expanding our offerings to include an academic aid program. This initiative is designed to support underprivileged students who face barriers to learning due to financial limitations.
Currently, we are developing a curriculum for core subjects to provide these students with academic resources, empowering them to achieve their educational goals.
Our Purpose
Our chamber is dedicated to serving the community by performing for non-profit organizations and hosting fundraising events to support local causes.
We believe that music should be accessible to everyone, regardless of who you are. We provide music lessons for youth and teens including those with and without financial needs or disabilities. Our inclusive environment allows all participants to express themselves, connect with others, and contribute to musical ensembles.
Through the transformative power of music, we aim to inspire personal growth, foster community involvement, and enrich the lives of all children.

Dear NWCC Families,
Happy Holidays! This is a season of gratitude, and I want to express my sincere appreciation for all of you. Thank you for your continued collaboration and support of NWCC.

More recently, we also performed at the Our Lady of Fatima.  See the link to Youtube (below) to see the example of the performance with NWCC and Northwest Seattle Catholic Choir!

JANUARY 2026 UPDATE
March 9, 2026 at 6:43:55 AM
Previous
Next
Dear NWCC family!
Happy New year! As we welcome 2026 - still very much in our wet season -I want to begin by sincerely thanking you for your continued engagement and support throughout last year.
We are deeply grateful and excited to move forward together into this new year.
Our first meeting in 2026 is Jan. 10th Saturday at 5pm. (5-7pm).
Starting 2026, I am excited to share an update regarding how NWCC recognizes students’ volunteer service.
In the past, NWCC applied for the Presidential Volunteer Service Award, which was based on an honor system.
As many families know, the PVSA program has been halted nationally, which unfortunately limited our students' opportunity to earn a nationally honored volunteer certification.
To continue recognizing our students’ meaningful service in a clear, credible, and structured way, we now find a new, nationally recognized volunteer system.
It operates at the same level of rigor and credibility as previous national programs.
Over winter break, NWCC successfully completed the qualification process and is now officially registered as a non-profit organization authorized to earn and verify volunteer service hours.
Here’s what this means for NWCC students:
Official Verification: NWCC is qualified to track and verify students’ volunteer hours this year. (from Sep. 2025 to Aug. 2026)
National Recognition: The award is recognized nationally and accepted by colleges and educational institutions as proof of verified volunteer service.
Structured Awards: Students’ service is evaluated based on total hours contributed.
NWCC‑Managed: All volunteer hours completed through NWCC programs will be tracked, verified, and submitted by NWCC to ensure proper recognition.
NWCC remains committed to our mission of “Bring Music and Education to All,” and we are proud to provide students with a meaningful and respected way to have their service recognized.
To help manage service hours, I will share each member’s earned volunteer hours at our upcoming meeting. We will also take time to brainstorm ways students can meet the required hours for this year’s award.
Below is additional information you may find helpful:
How are service hours verified?
NWCC maintains records of all student volunteer hours, including:
Date of service
Hours completed
Type of service (music outreach, education, community events, etc.)
This ensures all hours are accurately documented and eligible for national recognition.
What are the award levels?
Students are recognized based on the total number of verified service hours. Award levels match the thresholds previously used by the Presidential Volunteer Service Award.
*Hours are based on verified service completed within a 12-month period.
How will students receive the award?
NWCC submits all verified hours for national recognition.
Students receive an official certificate acknowledging their service.
Certificates can be included in school records, college applications, or scholarship portfolios.
Is this award recognized by colleges?
Yes. The award is nationally recognized and accepted by colleges and educational institutions as a verified volunteer honor. It highlights meaningful service and dedication, just like previous national volunteer awards.
Who manages the process?
NWCC manages the entire award process — tracking, verification, and submission — so families and students can focus on meaningful volunteer service.

NWCC JUNE UPDATES
June 1, 2025 at 1:06:08 AM
Previous
Next
Dear NWCC Families,
We are officially in June—rain or shine! It’s hard to believe we’ve reached the final month of the 2024–25 season. Thank you for supporting your children’s participation in the Northwest Collaborative Chamber and Choir, where they have grown not only in their musical talents but also in their service to the community.
I have three important updates to share with you:
Final Concert Information
Date: Saturday, June 7Time: 6:00 PM (Families and friends arrive)
Performer Call Time: 3:30 PM (Musicians arrive for rehearsal)
Dress Code: Black and white concert attire
Location:The Korean Kirkland Covenant Church14220 Juanita Woodinville Way NE, Kirkland, WA 98034
Dinner will be served for all student performers before the concert.We welcome and appreciate any parent help or food donations to support this effort. Please contact us if you are able to assist. Your generosity truly helps make the evening special for our young musicians!
Final NWCC Meeting – Last Day of the Season
Date: Saturday, June 14We will celebrate the end of the year and share the total number of service hours earned by our students. It will be a meaningful and joyful wrap-up to a wonderful season!
Important Update: President’s Volunteer Service Award (PVSA)
As an officially certified organization under both state and federal standards, NWCC has proudly conferred the President’s Volunteer Service Award (PVSA) to our students.
However, due to a recent decision by AmeriCorps, the PVSA program has been temporarily suspended as of May 27, 2025. At this time, all award issuance—including certificates and medals—has been halted nationwide for all certified organizations.More details: https://presidentialserviceawards.gov
This is part of a broader federal review of educational and volunteer service programs. There is currently no official timeline for when or how the PVSA will resume, though AmeriCorps will notify organizations directly if reinstated.
In the meantime, we’ve prepared meaningful alternatives to ensure our students’ service continues to be recognized:
NWCC Volunteer Service CertificateWe will issue an official certificate with total hours, service details, and dates. This can support college applications, school records, and scholarship portfolios.
Possibility of Retroactive PVSA RecognitionIn the past, PVSA has accepted retroactive applications for up to 12–24 months. We will help families keep accurate service records so we can apply promptly if the program resumes.
Continue Serving with Passion and PurposeThough a federal award is currently unavailable, we encourage our students to continue serving the community joyfully. Let’s uphold our goodwill and passion to contribute through music, knowing that true service makes a lasting impact and builds the leaders of tomorrow.
If you have any questions or need further information, please don’t hesitate to reach out.
Thank you again for your trust, your support, and your partnership throughout this meaningful season.
With warmest regards,
Jeongwon Hyun
Director of Education

Northwest Collaborative Chamber Newsletter
Time flies, and it is already the end of October.

November 15th (Saturday) at 4pm -  Performance at Ages Living Bellevue
(Address: 148 102nd Ave SE Bellevue WA 98004)

(Address: 3218 West Barrett st. Seattle, WA 98199)

Applause to our NWCC students for their leadership and dedication in sharing their talents with the community!

If you have not received your receipt by Nov. 22nd, please contact me directly to northwestcc.hyun@gmail.com.

Dear NWCC Family,
Spring has arrived, bringing cherry blossoms and tulips—even in the chilly weather! We have a few important announcements to share with you:
1. Spring Break (April 5 & 12, 2025)
We will observe Spring Break on April 5th and 12th. During these two weeks, there will be no chamber, choir, enrichment programs, or music lessons. Enjoy a restful break, and we’ll see you back on April 19th!
2. Collaborative Concert (Chamber) – April 19 & 20, 2025
Music Director Sung Lee has invited NWCC musicians to collaborate on a special performance for the Easter Mass at Our Lady of Fatima. Students who participate will earn extra service hours.
April 19 (Saturday), 6:30 – 10:00 PM
April 20 (Sunday), 8:00 – 10:00 AM
Interested students will travel to Our Lady of Fatima with Mr. Chung after our regular NWCC practice. More details will be shared soon.
3. Future Plans
May: We plan to host a community concert at a nursing home. If you know of a facility that would welcome an NWCC performance, please reach out!
June: Our final NWCC fundraising concert is in the works! We are considering an outdoor venue or a concert hall and will share details soon.
4. Tax Receipt for Donations
If you need a receipt for your donation, please send us the following information:
Student’s Name
Parent’s Name (Taxpayer)
Home Address
Email Address
I will email your receipt for your generous donation, which may qualify for tax benefits.
5. Enrichment Program Openings
We currently offer five enrichment groups:
Middle Math
Elementary Math
Creative Writing (Openings available)
Book Club (Openings available)
Spanish (Openings available)
If interested, please contact: Ashley Shim (Director of Enrichment Program): ashleyshim612@gmail.com Jeongwon (Education Director): northwestcc.hyun@gmail.com
Celebrating Achievements
We are proud of our NWCC musicians who have won competitions or been accepted into universities. Congratulations! Thank you for sharing your successes—they inspire our community.
Together, we continue our mission: Bringing Music and Education to All. Thank you for your dedication and support!
Best regards,
Jeongwon Hyun

Dear NWCC Family,
Seattle’s spring is quite versatile—rainy, haily, thundery, windy, sunny, then back to rain again! Let’s embrace this colorful season together.
Easter Mass at Our Lady of Fatima
Thank you to everyone who reached out about the Easter Mass concert at Our Lady of Fatima. We had six studentsparticipate in this special collaboration, and we were excited to see them work with other musicians for a shared cause. We’ll be sharing photos and videos of their performance soon!
Upcoming Events & Important Updates
1. Spring Break (April 5 & 12, 2025)
NWCC will be on Spring Break for two weeks (April 5 & 12). There will be no chamber, choir, enrichment programs, or music lessons during this time. Enjoy a restful break, and we’ll see you back on April 19th when all programs resume as usual.
2. Updated Schedule for April 19
Since we’ll be attending the Easter Mass at Our Lady of Fatima, NWCC practice will end early at 6:00 PM. No music lessons or sectionals will be held on this day. Please plan to pick up musicians by 6:00 PM. Regular scheduling will resume on April 26.
3. Community Concert at Kirkland Central Church (May 4, 2025)
NWCC’s Chamber and Choir have been invited to perform at Kirkland Central Church, where we regularly hold practice. We will perform three pieces during the Sunday Service. Afterward, the church community will provide a warm meal for our musicians.
Date: Sunday, May 4, 2025 Location: Kirkland Central Church Arrival: 10:30 AM (Education Hall) Service Begins: 11:00 AM Dress Code: Black & White, formal attire
Please confirm your availability by filling out the form: Sign-Up Form
4. Future Plans
May: We plan to host a community concert at a nursing home. If you know of a facility that would welcome an NWCC performance, please let us know!
June: Our final fundraising concert is in the works! We’re considering an outdoor venue or a concert hall and will provide more details soon.
Next Year (2025-26): NWCC has already received invitations to perform at various community events, including the WABA Korea 2025 Expo! Our group is gaining recognition, and we encourage all musicians to continue honing their skills for these exciting opportunities. For reference, check out last year’s WABA Korea 2024: WABA Expo
5. Celebrating Achievements
We are incredibly proud of our NWCC musicians who have won competitions or been accepted into universities! Your hard work and dedication inspire our entire community. Congratulations!
Continuing Our Mission
Together, we remain committed to Bringing Music and Education to All. Thank you for being part of NWCC—we appreciate your dedication and support!
Best regards,Jeongwon HyunNorthwest Collaborative Center

Important  Updates:
[Chamber Practice Schedule Notice]

4/4 (Sat): Tentatively No practice (Spring Break - to be finalized after a survey)

[New Korean Language Course]
We are excited to begin our Korean Language course next week! We currently have four students enrolled and three dedicated Teacher Assistant (TAs) to assist.
Our TAs are exceptional students who have achieved a Level 4 (the highest proficiency level) on the STAMP (Standards-Based Measurement of Proficiency) test and are on track to earn the Seal of Biliteracy. Combined with my experience as a certified K-12 World Language teacher (Korean) (with 5 years of experience of teaching Korean of various levels at the University of Washington and various Korean language schools), we are prepared to offer highly individualized instruction.
Goal: This course is designed to help high school students prepare for the STAMP test to earn high school world language credits without taking a year-long class. We will focus on vocabulary-building, reading comprehension, and writing skills.
Expansion: With our available TAs, we can now invite more students of various proficiency levels. If you are interested, please contact Mrs. Hyun to discuss how we can accommodate your child’s level.
Assessment: We will prepare assessment materials on Jan 30th to check each student's level. Please email me if you would like to participate so I can prepare enough materials.
[Korea Course Schedule - 10 Sessions]
The class will run from 4:00 PM to 4:50 PM starting January 31st.
TAs will receive 2 hours of service credit per week (1 hour for teaching and 1 hour for grading/feedback).

Dear NWCC family!
Happy New year! As we welcome 2026 - still very much in our wet season -I want to begin by sincerely thanking you for your continued engagement and support throughout last year.
We are deeply grateful and excited to move forward together into this new year.
Our first meeting in 2026 is Jan. 10th Saturday at 5pm. (5-7pm).
Starting 2026, I am excited to share an update regarding how NWCC recognizes students’ volunteer service.
In the past, NWCC applied for the Presidential Volunteer Service Award, which was based on an honor system.
As many families know, the PVSA program has been halted nationally, which unfortunately limited our students' opportunity to earn a nationally honored volunteer certification.
To continue recognizing our students’ meaningful service in a clear, credible, and structured way, we now find a new, nationally recognized volunteer system.
It operates at the same level of rigor and credibility as previous national programs.
Over winter break, NWCC successfully completed the qualification process and is now officially registered as a non-profit organization authorized to earn and verify volunteer service hours.
Here’s what this means for NWCC students:
Official Verification: NWCC is qualified to track and verify students’ volunteer hours this year. (from Sep. 2025 to Aug. 2026)
National Recognition: The award is recognized nationally and accepted by colleges and educational institutions as proof of verified volunteer service.
Structured Awards: Students’ service is evaluated based on total hours contributed.
NWCC‑Managed: All volunteer hours completed through NWCC programs will be tracked, verified, and submitted by NWCC to ensure proper recognition.
NWCC remains committed to our mission of “Bring Music and Education to All,” and we are proud to provide students with a meaningful and respected way to have their service recognized.
To help manage service hours, I will share each member’s earned volunteer hours at our upcoming meeting. We will also take time to brainstorm ways students can meet the required hours for this year’s award.
Below is additional information you may find helpful:
How are service hours verified?
NWCC maintains records of all student volunteer hours, including:
Date of service
Hours completed
Type of service (music outreach, education, community events, etc.)
This ensures all hours are accurately documented and eligible for national recognition.
What are the award levels?
Students are recognized based on the total number of verified service hours. Award levels match the thresholds previously used by the Presidential Volunteer Service Award.
*Hours are based on verified service completed within a 12-month period.
How will students receive the award?
NWCC submits all verified hours for national recognition.
Students receive an official certificate acknowledging their service.
Certificates can be included in school records, college applications, or scholarship portfolios.
Is this award recognized by colleges?
Yes. The award is nationally recognized and accepted by colleges and educational institutions as a verified volunteer honor. It highlights meaningful service and dedication, just like previous national volunteer awards.
Who manages the process?
NWCC manages the entire award process — tracking, verification, and submission — so families and students can focus on meaningful volunteer service.
WHO ARE WE?
The Northwest Collaborative Center (NWCC) is a nonprofit organization that serves our community through music. We create a positive and supportive environment where students can learn, grow, and work together. We are especially committed to making music education accessible to youth from underserved communities.

November 2025 News Letter
Northwest Collaborative Chamber Newsletter
Time flies, and it is already the end of October.
I hope all NWCC families are healthy and happy.
We have several important announcements in this newsletter.
1. Upcoming Performance
We are thrilled to announce the start of our Community Concert Series! Thank you all for your continued dedication and musicianship.
November 15th (Saturday) at 4pm -  Performance at Ages Living Bellevue
Address: 148 102nd Ave SE Bellevue WA 98004
Please arrive by 3:30pm for setup and tuning.
Dress code: Black and white formal attire.
Bring the music and music stand.
This is our first official community concert of the 2025-26 season.
Students will earn 3 service hours for this performance.
We are delighted to return to this venue after last Summer’s wonderful concert - they invited us back with great excitement!
November 22nd at 6:30pm -  Rehearsal practice at Our Lady of Fatima
Address: 3218 West Barrett st. Seattle, WA 98199
Please arrive by 6:15pm to the site for tuning.
This rehearsal is in preparation for our December performance.
Due to the Thanksgiving holiday, rehearsal will be held on-site on the 22nd.
Students will earn 3 service hours  for this rehearsal practice.
We’re happy to collaborate again with Our Lady of Fatima, who hosted us for the Easter concert last season.
December 4th (Thur) at 7pm Performance at Our Lady of Fatima
Address: 3218 West Barrett st. Seattle, WA 98199
Please arrive by 5:30pm for the dress rehearsal.
Dress code: Black and white formal attire.
Bring your music and music stand.
This is a collaborative fundraising concert with Our Lady of Fatima Parish.
Students will earn 5 service hours for this performance.
We are excited to return after last season’s Easter concert!
No regular practice on Dec. 6th (Sat) as we performed at Our Lady Fatima Parish on 4th (Thur).
No music lessons on November 15th (Sat), November 22nd (Sat), and December 6th (Sat) as we are not meeting at our regular practice location.
2. Community Outreach
The NWCC Outreach Team (Gracy, Jun, Kaila, Rachel and myself) has been diligently connecting with various community organizations to arrange our community concerts and fundraising events.
Applause to our NWCC students for their leadership and dedication in sharing their talents with the community!
3. Financial Update
The new NWCC bank account is now fully set up!
We transitioned to the new account due to a security issue, and all checks and annual donations have been successfully deposited.
Donation receipts will be sent by mid November.
If you have not received your receipt by Nov. 22nd, please contact me directly to northwestcc.hyun@gmail.com.
This is the new QR code that works with NWCC.
If you haven’t yet submitted your annual donation for the 2025-26 season, please use this new QR code to send it through your bank account.  We appreciate your support!
4. Open to New Musicians
NWCC is always welcoming new young musicians who wish to share their talent and serve the community through music.
If you have friends and classmates who might be interested, please invite them to join our NWCC chamber practice and performances!
Contact:
Vice-President of NorthWest Collaborative Chamber
Director of Education
Jeongwon Hyun  206.818.7869 (text)
northwestcc.hyun@gmail.com
